lessons.title: The family and the community

blocks.md: A **family** is a group of people who live together or are linked by blood, marriage or adoption, and who care for each other. Some families are **nuclear** (parents and children); others are **extended** (also grandparents, uncles, aunts and cousins), or have one parent. In every kind of family, members have **roles**: parents provide food, shelter, love and guidance; children learn, help and show respect.

blocks.caption: From me to the country
blocks.alt: Circles from me to the family, the community and the country.

blocks.title: Respect and cooperation
blocks.md: Good family life depends on **respect** (for parents, elders and each other), **honesty**, **sharing household tasks** (fetching water, cooking, sweeping, washing), **listening** to each other, and settling quarrels peacefully. Children also have a duty to study hard and keep themselves clean. Families that cooperate are stronger and happier.

Several families living near each other make a **community** (a village, a quarter or a neighbourhood). People in a community share a place, services and often customs. Community **services** include schools, health centres, markets, wells and water points, roads, churches and mosques, and the council. Good neighbours greet each other, help in difficulty (illness, funerals, building) and keep the surroundings clean.

blocks.title: How a pupil helps
blocks.md: At home: do chores, respect rules, care for younger children. In the community: keep the compound and streets clean, avoid noise, help old people, take part in communal work such as cleaning the market or clearing a path, and protect public property such as water taps and benches.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- A family is not defined only by the 'father, mother and children' model; many types exist and all deserve respect.
- Rights come with duties: a child has a right to care and a duty to help.
- 'Community' does not mean only one's own ethnic group: it means everyone who shares the place.

blocks.title: Example 1: type of family
blocks.statement: Mary lives with her mother, her grandmother and her two brothers in Kumba. What type of family is this?
steps: More than one generation lives together.
The grandmother is part of the household.
So it is an extended family.

blocks.title: Example 2: roles
blocks.statement: Give two duties a child has at home and two duties a parent has.
steps: Child: help with chores and respect parents.
Parent: provide food and shelter, and guide the child.
blocks.answer: Child: chores, respect. Parent: care and guidance.

blocks.md: A **school** is a community where pupils learn knowledge, skills and values. To work well it needs **rules**: about punctuality, uniform, behaviour, respect for teachers and property, and safety. Rules protect everyone's right to learn and make fair treatment possible. Rules are made by the school authorities, often with views from teachers, parents and pupils.

blocks.caption: What to do about bullying
blocks.alt: Four boxes showing the steps from seeing a problem to the school acting.

blocks.title: People in a school
blocks.md: The **principal** (head of the school) leads. **Vice principals** and **discipline masters** help to keep order. **Teachers** teach and guide. **Prefects** and class monitors help with order and are leaders among pupils. **Support staff** keep the school running. The **Parent–Teacher Association (PTA)** links families and school.

blocks.title: Rights and duties of a pupil
blocks.md: **Rights**: to be taught, to be treated with respect, to be protected from violence, to be heard and to take part in school activities. **Duties**: to attend regularly and arrive on time, to study, to obey school rules, to respect others, to keep the school clean and to take care of school property.

**Bullying** means repeatedly hurting or frightening someone weaker, by hitting, insults, threats, spreading rumours or leaving them out. It is wrong and harms both victims and bullies. What to do: **tell** a trusted adult, stay with friends, never take revenge or join in, and support a victim. Schools should have clear rules and fair sanctions; all pupils should help create a safe school.

blocks.title: Be careful
blocks.md:
- Obeying rules does not mean being silent when something is wrong: pupils may report problems politely to teachers.
- Prefects have authority but must be fair and respectful.
- Joking can become bullying if it hurts someone who asks you to stop.

blocks.title: Example 1: why a rule
blocks.statement: A school has a rule that pupils must arrive before 7:30 a.m. Give two reasons for this rule.
steps: Lessons start at a fixed time.
So the rule protects learning time and order.
blocks.answer: To start on time and avoid disturbing others.

blocks.title: Example 2: bullying
blocks.statement: A boy in your class is often insulted and isolated. What should you do?
steps: Do not join in the insults.
Tell a teacher or another trusted adult.
blocks.answer: Refuse to join in, report to a teacher and support the boy.
